messages.text: Saturday, November 7 · Canton, Michigan
Quiet overcast skies and the weight of a historic Senate election

The day brings a steady, gray chill to Canton as the region processes the recent election of the nation's first Muslim U.S. senator. Scientific inquiry meanwhile digs deep, linking Earth's mantle movements to long-lost geological history.
Expect an overcast day with a high of 46 degrees and a low of 34 degrees.
The sun rises at 7:15 AM and sets at 5:20 PM, with a waning crescent moon that is 4.3% illuminated.
Performances and benefit evenings

The Big Sky Company hosts a musical benefit for the ACLU at the North Star Lounge in Ann Arbor starting at 6 PM. Alternatively, you can attend a free performance of Jen Silverman's play Witch at the Keene Theater at 8 PM.
A community meeting is scheduled for the evening of November 11 at 6:30 PM.
Senate results and environmental policy shifts

Abdul El-Sayed has been elected to Michigan's open U.S. Senate seat, marking a historic national milestone. In related policy news, Congresswoman Debbie Dingell is preparing to introduce a Data Center Bill of Rights to address infrastructure and environmental concerns.
Looking toward the middle of next week
Mark your calendar for the meeting on November 11 at 6:30 PM.

Sunday, November 8 · Canton, Michigan
Henna art, classical oboe, and the quiet stillness of November

The day brings an overcast sky and a gentle chill, perfect for exploring local arts or settling into a quiet weekend rhythm. We look at the intersection of geological history and current environmental policy in the region.
Expect overcast conditions with a high near 57 degrees and a low around 32 degrees.
The sun rises at 7:16 AM and sets at 5:19 PM, with a new moon that is 1.3 percent illuminated.
A day for art and reflection
Experience henna art and community connection at the Betsy Barbour House starting at 2:00 PM. Later, Sara LeBlanc presents a master's degree oboe recital at the Earl V. Moore Building at 7:00 PM.
A meeting is scheduled for November 11 at 6:30 PM.
Regional shifts in policy and commerce

Congresswoman Debbie Dingell is proposing a Data Center Bill of Rights to address infrastructure and environmental concerns. Meanwhile, Ann Arbor's Blimpy Burger has officially reopened under new local ownership.
